extracted.intended_audience: readers of political biography / educated general public interested in political character
extracted.subtask_description: A character-study style guide describing the personal qualities, strengths, and defects that make an effective (or ineffective) political agitator/leader, illustrated by the career of Lord Brougham. Focuses on temperament, intellect, oratory, organization, and judicial aptitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive, impulsive disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: An aggressive, impulsive disposition that readily attacks abuses and rushes to reform; the opposite of immobility and sluggish conservatism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary to start reforms and denounce grievances; suits a multifarious agitator who must 'go off' and cannot live in a world without abuses. The text contrasts this with the English tendency to 'bear tranquilly the calamities of others.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Many‑sided excitability / miscellaneous activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An excitability that is many‑sided — stimulated by what is seen in the world rather than by solitary brooding — producing miscellaneous activity across numerous causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leads to continual action on diverse details; the agitator is quick to discern abuses in varied situations (law-courts, charities, royal scandals) and acts across many domains rather than concentrating on one doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty of easy anger (readiness to be angry)
rubrics_metrics.description: A readiness to anger — intolerance of complacency and attention to petty misfeasances — that drives the critique of officials and detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces sharp denunciations of administrative errors (misfiled documents, bad docketing) and makes the agitator 'the terror of a respectable administrator.' This temperament provokes professional jibes but fuels reform zeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeal for public welfare / disinterested action
rubrics_metrics.description: A principle of disinterested action: generous, often unselfish impulses and a rare zeal for the public good despite personal irritability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if partly temperamental, such impulses enable sustained public service; the text notes that behind the impulsiveness there is often a thread of calculation and discriminating judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspicuous labour / prolific, visible output
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity for conspicuous, prolific work — producing pamphlets, speeches, motions, and press material that keep the agitator constantly before the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not the same as the most exhausting verifying work, but the ability to supply motions, addresses, and a 'prodigious number' of written pieces is essential to keep an agitation alive and visible (example: filling shops with pamphlets and newspapers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extreme readiness / instantaneous responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Readiness to act at a moment's notice, correcting and producing material quickly when opportunities arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by Brougham's rapid press-management in elections and his ability to furnish many pieces and handbills in a few days; this facility supports agile political campaigning and leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skillful manipulation of men / leadership by insinuation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ability to manage, insinuate, and lead others — to place oneself at the head of opposition and bring reluctant men to his view by appearing to concur and opposing only partially at first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps conquer even unpopular groups; aided by an air of frankness that disarms suspicion (Sir James Mackintosh's anecdote).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational capacity / ability to marshal workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to keep numerous persons working under him and to gather the most recent facts, statistics, and details from many sources for immediate diffusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agitator needs an 'office' or organized body of labourers; the leader must assimilate and redistribute minutiae efficiently to influence public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extreme versatility / multi‑role competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Versatility to perform many different roles in a single day — courtroom advocate, hustings speaker, essayist, lecturer, judge, or popular educator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables sustained influence across institutions (Court, House of Lords, Mechanics' Institution, literary societies) and supports the agitator's varied career demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quickness in changing tasks ('changing his hand')
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility for rapidly switching mental modes and tasks — moving from forensic work to popular addresses to learned essays without loss of effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued by Adam Smith as a facility for intellectual labour; prevents stagnation in a single specialty and helps sustain multifarious activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enterprising intellect / intellectual courage
rubrics_metrics.description: Readiness to offer bold, general outlines of knowledge and to attempt an embracing conception of topics rather than ceding them to narrow specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellectual courage allows the agitator to sketch broad relations and make subjects intelligible to the man of the world, even at the risk of error; contrasted with the timidity of specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rough‑and‑ready oratory adapted to agitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Oratory that is rough, aggressive, sarcastic, and detail‑ready — effective for rousing and battering causes rather than for artistic perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May lack literary polish but suits a 'hundred-subject agitator' by providing immediate force and attack; abundant in sarcasm and vituperation tailored to practical agitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance of coarse methods / insensitivity of judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: A tolerance (or need) for coarse, non‑delicate modes of action and judgment; delicate, scrupulous judgment is less suited to the agitator who must err by excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delicate natures or highly sensitive nerves are likely to fail in dispersed, stormy agitational life; some coarseness and harshness help sustain public campaigning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harsh nerves as an asset
rubrics_metrics.description: Robustness of temperament — harsh nerves — which prevents shrinkage from the jarred, jangled life of agitation and allows continued usefulness despite strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three days out of six the sensitive frame might be jarred; insistence that harsh nerves can be essential for continual agitation and popular work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiency: want of a thinking (deliberative) intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: A lack of patient, cautious, philosophic deliberation and slow inquiry — unsuited to the careful reflecting intellect — as a potential defect of the agitator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The life of a miscellaneous agitator excludes the patient philosopher who would investigate while others attack; speed and sanguinity are prioritized over hesitation and scruple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiency: poor delicate/tactful advocacy (striking wrong)
rubrics_metrics.description: A tendency to strike hard but sometimes wrongly in forensic practice — an imperfect tact and discretion as an advocate, despite adequate legal attainments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical success at the bar may be large, but finer advocacy (winning delicate verdicts) may elude such a temperament (example: Scarlett 'stole verdicts away' from Brougham).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession of a 'daemonic' or dangerous element
rubrics_metrics.description: A mischievous excitability or 'devil' — a glare of danger in the eye — that makes the person formidable and unpredictable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard to describe but physiognomically evident; a little of this 'demon' is declared excellent for an agitator though it can make the person unpleasant in difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two kinds of judicial excellence (judging for parties vs for lawyers)
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard distinguishing great judges: (a) 'judges for the parties' who decide particular cases rightly by acute fact-finding and (b) 'judges for the lawyers' who expound broad principles applicable to future disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate Lord Brougham: he is shown to be an adequate lawyer and judge in many respects but not of the absolutely judicial, essay-like cast that supplies ample exposition for posterity; this distinction serves as an evaluative rubric for judicial quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between conspicuous agitation and deeper verifying labour
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that visible, multifarious agitation (speeches, pamphlets, motions) differs from the more exhausting, verifying, scrutinizing labour of detailed inquiry; both require energy but are distinct skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conspicuous labour carries movements far, but the last verifying touches and heavy scrutiny are more wearing; an effective agitator must manage the trade-off between breadth of activity and depth of verification.
